final_answer: The greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm by trapping heat. Solar energy reaches Earth, warming the surface, which emits infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases like CO₂ absorb this infrared radiation, vibrate, and re-emit energy in all directions—some back toward Earth, some outward. This process enhances warming. CO₂ absorbs infrared in specific wavelengths due to molecular structure, then emits photons randomly. This re-emission is key to the greenhouse effect.
